html:
SMTO-LLM-0033 — Model returned invalid JSON

GUID: cc5078bb-13da-4e3a-afe7-7ae07e481a2b
Slug: llm-invalid-json
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • SMTO needed the answer in an exact fill-in-the-blanks format. The model's reply was broken or incomplete in that format, so SMTO couldn't read it and did not act on it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and select Check saved model. The check asks for one small answer in the exact format, so a failure shows the model can't reliably produce it.
  2. In the same card, open Limits and recovery and make sure Output allowance isn't set very low. Raise it if needed and select Save Main. An answer that is cut off before it finishes leaves the format broken.
  3. If it keeps failing, ask the person who runs your model service whether this model supports tool calling, or pick a model that does and start a new task. Some models or server setups can't produce the exact format SMTO needs.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model reports passed, and the task's next step completes without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your model service. Don't resend the same request over and over; change the model or its settings first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A structured model response could not be decoded: GET /models returned non-JSON during model auto-discovery, the completion content held no complete JSON object, or the named-result tool arguments were not a valid JSON object.

What this means

  • JSON decoding or required object extraction failed in model discovery, answer content or named-result arguments; a readable text response need not be valid structured data. This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • JSON decoding or required object extraction failed in model discovery, answer content or named-result arguments; a readable text response need not be valid structured data.

How to diagnose it

  • Locate the recorded parsing stage and check the expected object shape and completion state; do not confuse malformed discovery metadata with a malformed tool argument.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the raw response preview and validation_stage in the error details. Confirm the serving stack supports structured output for this model (a matching tool-call parser or guided decoding on vLLM, JSON mode on hosted APIs) and that the output allowance is large enough that answers aren't cut off; if discovery failed, check that <base_url>/models returns the OpenAI-compatible model list.
  • Use a provider with the required structured response support and inspect its response-format configuration.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The response at that stage parses as the required complete JSON value without repairing or guessing missing fields.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • This category concerns model preparation or response acceptance. It does not reverse earlier operations or establish their outcome; their receipts remain authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
